newsitem.title: UK: A victory for T-bonds on the charts, target at 118.
newsitem.headline: A victory for T-bonds on the charts, target at 118.

text.p: Treasury bond futures will forge ahead seeking to retest levels not seen since February, as the market recieves a U.S. election boost, technical analysts said on Wednesday.
T-bonds can climb nearly four points in the weeks ahead, although they may pause for a while around 116-00 on the way, they said.
"What probably happened (in the elections) is what's best for the market," said Tom Hobson, director of technical analysis at Merrill Lynch in London.
"Bonds have taken out key resistance at 114-00 and the market is heading up to 116-00 and then on to 118-00."
At 0751 GMT, December T-bond futures were at 114-09 in automated trade, up half a point from Tuesday's Chicago settlement.
On continuation charts, 116-00 was the low on February 20, while 116-03 was the high on March 6, just before the market was stunned by February non-farm payrolls data which showed a large rise.
The 118-00 level is just below the high on February 20 at 118-03.
David Wood, an independent technical analyst near London, set upside targets in a range between 115-30 and 116-16.

"The market seems to be taking the election well at the moment but it will be tough for it to get up to there quickly. Maybe over the next month to six weeks, or through to the end of the year," he said.
Wood was cautious about getting too bullish.

"People may be subscribing to a re-test of highs of 120-00 plus, but I can't see that," he said. "It all looks strong at the moment and the easiest thing would be call it a lot higher but I will stay with the idea it will top out around 116-00."
He said the 115-30 and 116-16 range reflected a number of resistances from long-term charts and targets from the current upmove.
December T-bonds have recently rallied from a low of 105-09 on September 6 to a high at 114-15 in automated trade since Tuesday's settlement.
Continuation charts show T-bonds reached a high at 115-30 on October 6, 1995, and a low at 116-16 twice in October 1995.
Marc Ostwald, technical strategist at London Bond Broking Company here, said T-bonds had finally broken free of a bear grip.
"The whole downtrend has really been broken. The question is where to we go from here?"
He said the rally from October 1995 gave a good indication of what to expect. "We ran straight up from 112-00 and the real first stop we got to was 117-23," Ostwald said.
He said initial resistance was around 116-00.
"I would expect this in the medium term to run up to 116-00 and if it's got enough momentum behind it I don't see why it shouldn't run up to 117-23," he said.
In the near term, he said the key was for T-bonds to break through the 114-24,26 area, which he said was roughly equivalent to a 6.5 percent yield on the long bond.
Wood said for Wednesday's session T-bonds would struggle just short of 115-00 as they needed to consolidate before tackling the longer term targets.
"The 114-20 to 114-30 area will be difficult," he said. "A collection of targets from the short-term current move and a decent high made in March come together in that zone."
On the downside support will be offered between 114-06 and 113-28. Below there the contract would start to weaken, he said.
"A break of 113-16 would be quite significant for hourly charts and in the short-term T-bonds could get back down to the mid-112s," said Wood.
